<p dir="auto">KomaMRI.jl is a Julia package for highly efficient ⚡ MRI simulations. KomaMRI was built from the ground up to be: easy to use, extensible, cross-platform, and powered by open-source community standards.</p>
<div align="center" dir="auto">
<markdown-accessiblity-table><table>
<tbody><tr>
<td rowspan="2" width="50%"><a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="./docs/src/assets/ui-simulation.gif"><img width="100%" src="./docs/src/assets/ui-simulation.gif" data-animated-image="" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></td>
<td align="left" width="50%"><b>Features:</b></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td align="left">
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Fast simulations with CPU/GPU parallelization 🏃💨</li>
<li>Extensible, so anyone can include new features 🆙</li>
<li>Supports community-standards <a href="##" title="Pulseq and ISMRMRD">🤝</a></li>
<li>Interactive visualizations using PlotlyJS.jl 📲</li>
<li>Cross-platform (Windows, Mac &amp; Linux) 🌐</li>
<li>Friendly GUI (using web technologies) 😌</li>
<li>Compatible with modern notebooks <a href="##" title="Pluto and Jupyter">🎈</a></li>
<li>Flexible API for advanced users 👨‍💻</li>
</ul>
</td>
</tr>
</tbody></table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
</div>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 class="heading-element" dir="auto">News</h2><a id="user-content-news" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: News" href="#news"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>(29 Aug 2024)</strong> Our first GSoC student, Ryan Kierulf, presented his fantastic work at the JuliaHealth monthly meeting 🥳! (presentation available <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R6Z20G0J4bM" rel="nofollow">here</a>) More info in the docs: <a href="https://juliahealth.org/KomaMRI.jl/dev/explanation/4-gpu-explanation/" rel="nofollow">GPU Parallelization</a>, <a href="https://juliahealth.org/KomaMRI.jl/dev/how-to/4-run-distributed-simulations/" rel="nofollow">Distributed Simulations</a> and <a href="https://juliahealth.org/JuliaHealthBlog/posts/ryan-gsoc/Ryan_GSOC.html" rel="nofollow">Ryan's JuliaHealth blog</a></li>
<li><strong>(7 Dec 2023)</strong> Koma was present in <a href="https://mritogether.esmrmb.org/" rel="nofollow">MRI Together</a> 😼. The talk is available <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9mRQH8um4-A" rel="nofollow">here</a>. Also, I uploaded the promised <a href="https://juliahealth.org/KomaMRI.jl/stable/tutorial-pluto/01-gradient-echo-spin-echo/" rel="nofollow">educational example</a>.</li>
<li><strong>(17 Nov 2023)</strong> Pretty excited of being part of <a href="https://github.com/pulseq/ISMRM-Virtual-Meeting--November-15-17-2023">ISMRM Pulseq's virtual meeting</a>. The slides available <a href="https://github.com/pulseq/ISMRM-Virtual-Meeting--November-15-17-2023/blob/35a8da7eaa0bf42f2127e1338a440ccd4e3ef53c/slides/day3_KomaMRI_simulator_Quantitative_MRI.pdf">here</a>.</li>
<li><strong>(27 Jul 2023)</strong> I gave a talk at MIT 😄 for <a href="https://juliacon.org/2023/" rel="nofollow">JuliaCon 2023</a>! A video of the presentation can be seen <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WVT9wJegC6Q" rel="nofollow">here</a>.</li>
<li><strong>(29 Jun 2023)</strong> <a href="https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mrm.29635" rel="nofollow">KomaMRI.jl's paper</a> was chosen as a July editor's pick in MRM 🥳!</li>
<li><strong>(6 Mar 2023)</strong> Paper published in MRM 😃!</li>
<li><strong>(8 Dec 2022)</strong> <a href="https://github.com/JuliaHealth/KomaMRI.jl/releases/tag/v0.7.0">KomaMRI v0.7</a>: improved performance (<strong>5x faster</strong>), type stability, extensibility, and more!</li>
<li><strong>(17 May 2022)</strong> <a href="https://archive.ismrm.org/2022/2815.html" rel="nofollow">ISMRM 2022 digital poster</a> presented in London, UK. Recording <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tH_XUnoSJK8" rel="nofollow">here!</a>. Name change <a href="https://github.com/JuliaHealth/KomaMRI.jl/releases/tag/v0.6.0">MRIsim.jl -&gt; KomaMRI.jl</a>.</li>
<li><strong>(Aug 2020)</strong> <a href="https://github.com/JuliaHealth/KomaMRI.jl/releases/tag/v0.2.1-alpha">Prehistoric version</a> of Koma, MRIsim, presented as an <a href="https://cds.ismrm.org/protected/20MProceedings/PDFfiles/4437.html" rel="nofollow">ISMRM 2020 digital poster</a> (virtual conference).</li>
</ul>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 class="heading-element" dir="auto">Installation</h2><a id="user-content-installation" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Installation" href="#installation"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">To install, just <strong>type</strong> <code>] add KomaMRI</code> in the Julia REPL or copy-paste the following into the Julia REPL:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-julia notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="pkg&gt; add KomaMRI
pkg&gt; add CUDA     # Optional: Install desired GPU backend (CUDA, AMDGPU, Metal, or oneAPI)
"><pre>pkg<span class="pl-k">&gt;</span> add KomaMRI
pkg<span class="pl-k">&gt;</span> add CUDA     <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Optional: Install desired GPU backend (CUDA, AMDGPU, Metal, or oneAPI)</span>
</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">For more information about installation instructions, refer to the section <a href="https://JuliaHealth.github.io/KomaMRI.jl/dev/how-to/1-getting-started" rel="nofollow">Getting Started</a> of the documentation.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 class="heading-element" dir="auto">First run</h2><a id="user-content-first-run" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: First run" href="#first-run"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">KomaMRI.jl features a convenient GUI with predefined simulation inputs (i.e. <code>Sequence</code>, <code>Phantom</code>, and <code>Scanner</code>). To launch the GUI, use the following command:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-julia notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="using KomaMRI
using CUDA        # Optional: Load GPU backend (default: CPU)
KomaUI()"><pre><span class="pl-k">using</span> KomaMRI
<span class="pl-k">using</span> CUDA        <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Optional: Load GPU backend (default: CPU)</span>
<span class="pl-c1">KomaUI</span>()</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Press the button that says "Simulate!" to do your first simulation :). Then, a notification will emerge telling you that the simulation was successful. In this notification, you can either select to (1) see the Raw Data or (2) to proceed with the reconstruction.</p>
<div class="markdown-alert markdown-alert-important" dir="auto"><p class="markdown-alert-title" dir="auto"><svg class="octicon octicon-report mr-2" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M0 1.75C0 .784.784 0 1.75 0h12.5C15.216 0 16 .784 16 1.75v9.5A1.75 1.75 0 0 1 14.25 13H8.06l-2.573 2.573A1.458 1.458 0 0 1 3 14.543V13H1.75A1.75 1.75 0 0 1 0 11.25Zm1.75-.25a.25.25 0 0 0-.25.25v9.5c0 .138.112.25.25.25h2a.75.75 0 0 1 .75.75v2.19l2.72-2.72a.749.749 0 0 1 .53-.22h6.5a.25.25 0 0 0 .25-.25v-9.5a.25.25 0 0 0-.25-.25Zm7 2.25v2.5a.75.75 0 0 1-1.5 0v-2.5a.75.75 0 0 1 1.5 0ZM9 9a1 1 0 1 1-2 0 1 1 0 0 1 2 0Z"></path></svg>Important</p><p dir="auto">Starting from <strong>KomaMRI v0.9</strong> we are using <a href="https://pkgdocs.julialang.org/v1/creating-packages/#Conditional-loading-of-code-in-packages-(Extensions)" rel="nofollow">package extensions</a> to deal with GPU dependencies, meaning that to run simulations on the GPU, installing (<code>add CUDA/AMDGPU/Metal/oneAPI</code>) and loading (<code>using CUDA/AMDGPU/Metal/oneAPI</code>) the desired backend will be necessary (see <a href="https://JuliaHealth.github.io/KomaMRI.jl/dev/explanation/4-gpu-explanation" rel="nofollow">GPU Parallelization</a> and <a href="#tested-compatibility">Tested compatibility</a>).</p>
</div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 class="heading-element" dir="auto">How to Contribute</h2><a id="user-content-how-to-contribute" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: How to Contribute" href="#how-to-contribute"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">KomaMRI exists thanks to all our contributors:</p>
<a href="https://github.com/JuliaHealth/KomaMRI.jl/graphs/contributors">
  <img src="https://camo.githubusercontent.com/fd40a00f4eb57687333ea84b84074bfce0ade10de48a31bf7ae61b522bb51290/68747470733a2f2f636f6e747269622e726f636b732f696d6167653f7265706f3d4a756c69614865616c74682f4b6f6d614d52492e6a6c" height="40px" data-canonical-src="https://contrib.rocks/image?repo=JuliaHealth/KomaMRI.jl" style="max-width: 100%;">

<p dir="auto">Want to be highlighted here? We welcome contributions from the community! If you're interested in contributing, please read our <a href="CONTRIBUTING.md">Contribution Guidelines</a> for details on how to get started.</p>
